newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria parties sign pact at disputed conference.
newsitem.headline: Algeria parties sign pact at disputed conference.

text.p: Thirty-eight Algerian politicians and other leaders on Sunday signed a pact at a disputed national conference to pave the way for a multi-party system and general elections next year.

President Liamine Zeroual was shown live on Algerian television applauding those who signed at the conference, which was boycotted by two main secular parties and from which radical Islamists were barred.
The pact was intended to end nearly five years of violence, blamed on fundamentalists, in which some 50,000 people have been killed.
Algeria's "National Conference of Understanding" follows nearly two years of tortuous talks, and a largely boycotted similar conference in January 1994.

Outside the conference hall, in the Palais des Nations 20 km (12 miles) from the capital Algiers, heavily armed troops, gendarmerie and police gave visible evidence of the perceived need to guard against Moslem fundamentalists.
Zeroual was appointed in January 1994 as head of state and confirmed in the post by Algeria's first multi-candidate presidential poll last November.
He told the opening session on Saturday that the meeting aimed at "finding a real solution for the causes of the recent downward spiral which almost put in peril the future of our country".
But residents of Algiers said there was little public interest in the meeting. "We have heard of talks to resolve the crisis so many times before," said one.

Boualem Benhamouda, head of the former ruling National Liberation Front (FLN), said on Saturday: "The authorities are also called to lay down the right conditions to hold legislative and local elections by ensuring equal opportunities for the parties..."
Benhamouda's party is seen as the main one taking part, alongside the legal Hamas movement, whose leader Mafhoud Nahnah won more than 2.9 million votes in November's presidential election.

Abdallah Djaballah, leader of Ennahda, another legal Islamist party, called on Zeroual to free all detained militants and end the state of emergency imposed in February 1992 which politicians say has effectively frozen party activity.
The emergency was imposed after violence erupted following the authorities' cancellation of a general election in which the now-banned Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) had taken a huge lead.
Zeroual, who told the gathering that "abject terrorism has been firmly rejected by the Algerian people", said Algeria "has to face the next election dates to complete its institutional structures".
He was referring to a referendum to change the constitution which he plans within three months and his pledge to hold general and local elections next year.
